comment: Client/server test scenarios. A scenario with server and client plugs runs as two processes through run_client_server_test.sh (SCENARIO=<name>, or run_scenarios.sh for all of them); one with a host plug is a single process that spawns its own client (the CI dummy plug jobs). compare_journals.py --scenario <name> checks the journals against the scenario's expect block. Every field but the plugs is optional. networks lists the network profiles (below) a scenario must pass under, default lan; a profile's lag_ms (round trip), jitter_ms and loss_pct are simulated on the client (--net-lag etc.), and its tolerance loosens the comparison. expect: objects = replicated objects the server spawned, in_play = players in play in every dump, hits = hits the server decided, grabs = grab state changes on each client, all minimums; tolerance overrides the comparison tolerances (position and object_position in world units, clock_us).

lossy.description: Some delay, and packets lost both ways

default.description: Join, spawn and agree on the roster

scenario.description: Both walk around, then the server switches to beavercreek

spawn.description: Server spawns replicate; client requests are accepted or rejected

fire.description: Both players shoot each other; shots relayed, hits decided by the server

grab.description: The client forge-grabs a rifle the server spawned

vehicle.description: Ghost bolts from the server, warthog chaingun from the client

census.description: The client drops the spawn backlog and a despawn; the object census repairs both

pause.description: The server pauses; the client stops on the same tick

net_multiplayer.description: Self-contained host with a spawned client, map switch mid-session

net_splitscreen.description: As net_multiplayer, with a second split screen seat on each side
